newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico arrests drug lord as U.S. drug review looms.
newsitem.headline: Mexico arrests drug lord as U.S. drug review looms.

text.p: The Mexican government on Thursday announced the arrest of a top drug kingpin, just hours before Washington was due to "certify" whether Mexico is collaborating in the war on illegal narcotics.
Oscar Malherbe de Leon, the acting head of the Gulf or Matamoros drugs cartel, was arrested in a joint operation by police and the Defense Ministry, the Attorney General's Office said in a statement.

"The arrest has been achieved of Oscar Malherbe de Leon, who, since the arrest of Juan Garcia Abrego, has been at the head of the drug-trafficking operations of the so-called Gulf Cartel," the statement said.
Malherbe tried and failed to buy his release by offering a $2 million bribe to the arresting officers, it added.
The announcement came as the United States neared the deadline for deciding whether Mexico is cooperating in its antinarcotics battle.
President Bill Clinton must decide by Saturday whether to "certify" the anti-drugs efforts of Mexico and 31 other countries. Countries that fail the annual U.S. review may face U.S. sanctions.

Although Mexico has always received the approval of Washington in the past, its full "certification" was thrown into doubt last week following the arrest of its anti-drugs czar on drugs corruption charges.
Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo was fired as head of the National Institute for Combating Drugs and charged with working for Amado Carrillo Fuentes, head of the powerful Juarez drugs cartel.
The Mexican government says it does not need "certification" by the United States or anyone else to prove its commitment to fighting drug-trafficking.

The Gulf cartel is believed to have lost power in recent years as Carrillo's strength has grown. The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration has called Carrillo the most powerful drug-trafficker in Mexico.
The other major Mexican drugs gang, apart from the Juarez and Gulf groups, is the Tijuana cartel headed by the Arellano Felix brothers.
At the time of his arrest Malherbe was carrying a .45 pistol, the Attorney General's Office said.
It gave no details of when or where Malherbe was captured but said his arrest was the result of an operation begun in May last year.
"In the coming hours the detainee will be taken to the corresponding jail and placed at the disposal of the relevant federal judge," the statement said.
Malherbe was arrested on murder and drug-trafficking charges and would now also face bribery charges, it added.
His former boss, Garcia Abrego, was arrested near the northern Mexican city of Monterrey in January last year and immediately deported to the United States, where he was born.
He is now serving 11 life sentences without parole in a U.S. prison after being found guilty in a Houston court of shipping millions of dollars worth of cocaine into the United States.

The Attorney General's Office said the operation had almost managed to arrest Malherbe once before in the northern town of Tamaulipas. It said he was also wounded in a shoot-out with authorities in 1994 and hospitalized for several weeks in Texas under a false name.
